attributes.probed_form: NO SOURCE CHANGE. The predecessor record's diagnosis was correct and its prescription — that closing this needs 'a value-equality/copy-propagation proof mode, a genuinely new guard surface' — was executed. What it got wrong is the SHAPE of that mode, and the correction is the transferable part. The predecessor proposed substituting a same-valued register at the refusing use (f27 for f4 at +0xc4), i.e. a SINGLE-STREAM value web on our side. That is unsound here and was measured so: our f27 IS redefined inside the loop (at +0x13c and +0x16c), so our f4 and f27 are NOT equal on the second iteration, and a single-stream copy-web analysis correctly refuses. The correct mode is RELATIONAL. verify_value_equality_recolor carries a RELATION R between our registers and target registers with the invariant '(a,b) in R => our a and the target's b hold the same value here', seeded with the identity at entry, narrowed at every definition (a define retires every (ours,*) and (*,target) pair), intersected at joins, and CLOSED OVER VALUE-PRESERVING COPIES in both streams: after `our: d<-s` every target register value-equal to s is value-equal to d, and symmetrically. That closure is what lets one value replicated across five registers in each stream be matched up in whichever way the two allocators chose. The mode is opt-in per rule, never runs unless the strict proof has already failed, refuses if the strict proof SUCCEEDS (a stale declaration must be removed, not left resting on the wider mode), refuses to compose with unproven_recolor_audit or with a post-recolor permutation, and requires every escape it takes to be DECLARED — an undeclared escape and a declared-but-unused escape are both errors, so a rule cannot widen silently and a source change that moves the residual fails the build.

The 18 substitutions are two replicated-constant webs: the zero from `lfs lbl_80345EC8` (ours f4,f30,f29,f28,f27 against the target's f29,f28,f27,f26,f5) and the constant from `lfs lbl_80346030` (ours f0,f31 against the target's f30,f0). The 2 exchanges are a SECOND, distinct mechanism found only by building the first: at +0x1d0 and +0x51c the two streams pass fcmpu's operands in opposite order. Operand exchange swaps the FL and FG bits of the result field and leaves FE and FU untouched, so it is equivalence-preserving exactly when every consumer reads only EQ or SO; both sites are consumed solely by a bne/beq, and that is PROVED by a CR-bit liveness walk (any ordering branch, mcrf, mfcr, CR-logical, or a field live at exit refuses), not declared by hand.
